thread:
morgan: Heads-up: customer reported weird quota + billing mismatch when a streaming session truncated, a toolcall ran, and routing rolled mid-stream. they got a provisional spike and then a quota breach alert.
tess: ugh. can you paste minimal logs?
morgan: session=zz-999 model=redwood-2 route=canary-A at 2026-03-22T15:14:02Z. short trace: 
```
15:14:02 REQ sess=zz-999 route=canary-A prefix_tokens=19
15:14:04 STREAM_TRUNC sess=zz-999 trunc_tokens=2 provisional=true prov_id=p-67
15:14:04 TOOLCALL start sess=zz-999 tool=kb_lookup
15:14:04 TOOLCALL end sess=zz-999 tool_tokens=7
15:14:05 ROUTE_ROLLOUT applied canary-B
15:14:05 RECONNECT sess=zz-999 route=canary-B
15:14:06 QUOTA_CHECK sess=zz-999 allow=false reason=quota_exceeded confirmed_usage=98
15:14:07 STREAM_RESUME sess=zz-999 resumed_tokens=24 confirmed=true confirm_ref=p-67
15:14:07 BILL provisional: 19+2 route=canary-A
15:14:08 BILL confirmed: 24+7 route=canary-B
```
morgan: UI shows provisional (21) + confirmed (31) -> apparent 52 tokens. customer was also blocked by quota in the middle.
harry: two problems: (1) provisional emission prematurely influencing customer-facing quota meter, (2) confirmer matching not collapsing provisional+confirm when route changes. both combine to create noisy/incorrect UX.
quota-bot: Alert: provisional_causes_quota_block detected sess=zz-999 delta=2 :no_entry_sign: :money_with_wings:
tess: we intentionally surfaced provisional to help customers approximate costs in realtime. but it's dangerous if provisional both shows and counts toward hard quota enforcement. we need a principled semantics decision.
lucy: options: A) provisional is purely informative (no quota impact) and quota decisions only consider confirmed; B) provisional counts toward a soft quota that triggers warnings but not hard blocks; C) keep current behavior but make routing handoffs guarantee provisional->confirm idempotency so quota counts don't double dip.
dev: engineering thoughts: A is safest for correctness. customers who depend on provisional to throttle can opt-in with an account flag. Implementation: small change: make quota checks read from committed ledger and a separate provisional estimate store. Also mark provisional ledger rows as "non-blocking" so enforcement ignores them.
morgan: downside: some customers (esp. small teams) use provisional to avoid overage surprises. removing its enforcement breaks their workflow. opt-in flag seems reasonable.
harry: on confirmer side we should implement a prov_group_id that survives route swaps. right now we key by (session, route, seq) which breaks when route changes. prov_group_id on first provisional emission (p-67) and included on all subsequent events would let confirmer collapse provisional + confirmed across routes.
tess: agree. steps: 1) change provisional emission to generate prov_group_id and persist with provisional row (small) 2) propagate prov_group_id through routing handoff payloads so fallback preserves it (small) 3) update confirmer to lookup by prov_group_id first and collapse provisionals into a reconciliation delta (medium) 4) backend: change quota decision to ignore provisional rows unless account flag is set (small) 5) console: show both net-confirmed usage and provisional estimates with a badge that clarifies quota semantics (small UI).
quota-bot: Info: provisional_flag_safety_patch created id=QS-890
lucy: telemetry: add metric provisional_vs_confirm_delta per-customer + provisional_causes_quota_block_count and routing_rollout_rate tag. also add a dashboard panel for canary rollouts showing provisional spikes.
dev: tests: unit tests for confirmer lookup by prov_group_id, e2e for route-swap + toolcall + multiple truncs, and quota tests for default-off provisional-enforcement. add a chaos test where routing handoff drops prov_group_id to ensure fallback logic tolerates missing ids.
morgan: backfill: support asked for a one-off reconciliation for the impacted account. we should provide an ops script that matches provisionals with confirms across routes by time-window and prov_group_id where present, and create adjustments where mismatch found. can we run a targeted backfill?
harry: yes. I'll write backfill that scans session range, matches by session + time overlap and prov metadata, and emits adjustment rows flagged as manually_reconciled. ops can run for that customer tomorrow.
tess: owners: dev -> implement prov_group_id & confirmer changes; lucy -> telemetry + dashboard; product -> decision on default provisional quota behavior (we recommend default: provisional does not block quota); support -> coordinate backfill run.
quota-bot: Reminder: provisional_backfill_requested for acct=acct-714 ticket=SUP-812
morgan: thanks team. please link PRs here. I'll update support to hold on refunds until backfill completes. :thumbsup:
